item.title: Saudi, Israeli leaders try to shape Trump's decisions on Iran conflict
item.description: As conflict potentially expands in the region, Trump met with the Saudi defense minister and with Benjamin Netanyahu. The Israeli prime minister counseled Trump on three options for the war.

item.title: First responders testify in Lindsay Clancy murder trial
item.description: First responders testified Thursday in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, who admitted to killing her three children but pleaded not guilty to three counts of first-degree murder. CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul has the details.

item.title: Stocks rebound as some tech companies rally
item.description: Wall Street saw a big rebound on Thursday, with the Dow and Nasdaq shooting up more than 600 points. Yahoo Finance senior reporter Brooke DiPalma joins with analysis.

item.title: Spain deploys military to Morocco border after migrant crossings, 9 deaths
item.description: Spain will deploy its military to Ceuta to help restore order at its border with Morocco after local authorities in Ceuta had asked the central government in Madrid for reinforcements.

item.title: Online seller of peptides is sentenced to nearly 6 years in prison
item.description: A federal judge sentenced the owner of a peptide company to nearly six years in prison after finding the business deceived customers and sold products that were adulterated with steroids.

item.title: CD vs. high-yield savings account: Which is better to open this August?
item.description: Both accounts have unique advantages in today's economy. Here's what to consider before making a final decision.

item.title: 4 major Latino organizations joining forces to mobilize voters for midterms
item.description: CBS News has learned that four of the nation's largest Latino civic organizations are joining forces for the first time, combining their voter outreach operations ahead of the crucial 2026 midterms.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy triple murder scene "turned very chaotic, very quickly," paramedic testifies
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is facing three first-degree murder charges, accused of killing her children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in 2023. Thursday was the third day of witness testimony.

item.title: Iran war appears to expand to Egypt's coast as drones hit gas port
item.description: Drone strikes hit gas vessels at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean, as a poll shows little American support for the five-month war with Iran.

item.title: Mortgage rates hit highest level in a year amid inflation fears
item.description: Mortgage rates are drifting higher as the Fed's interest rate decision and war in the Middle East fuel inflation concerns.

item.title: Most Americans believe war with Iran is not worth fighting, AP poll says
item.description: A poll from the Associated Press shows that two-thirds of Americans believe the Iran war is not worth fighting. CBS News chief white house correspondent Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Details on Colin Gray's 15-year sentence for son's Appalache High School shooting
item.description: Colin Gray, father of Appalache High School shooter Colt Gray, was sentenced to 15 years in prison on Thursday for his part in the 2024 tragedy perpetrated by his son. CBS News legal contributor Rebecca Roiphe has more.

item.title: Afghan woman to fight U.S. efforts to deport her over "alien terrorist" claim
item.description: Nazira Haji Zada's lawyer argued that the Justice Dept. is violating her due process rights.

item.title: Senate committee advances Dr. Erica Schwartz to be Trump's CDC director
item.description: If confirmed by the full Senate, Dr. Erica Schwartz would become the 22nd director of the Atlanta-based Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Want to save on student loan payments? Here's how to get a discount.
item.description: Federal student loan borrowers can qualify for a 1% discount on monthly interest charges if they enroll by the deadline. Here's what to know.

item.title: Grants halted at agency devoted to safety of U.S. healthcare
item.description: Congress appropriated $345 million for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality for the 2026 fiscal year, but the agency has spent less than $15 million on grants.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial centers on ex's 911 call: "She killed the kids"
item.description: Prosecutors allege Lindsay Clancy made a "calculated decision" in killing her kids, while the defense says she was overmedicated and suffering from extreme postpartum psychosis.

item.title: Why are workers at leading AI companies calling for a slowdown in AI development?
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other AI leaders say they support pacing the rapid advancement of AI's capabilities.

item.title: FTC sues Hims & Hers, alleging it shared health data with Meta, Snap
item.description: Telehealth platform disclosed users' "most private" health info and locked consumers into subscriptions, regulators allege.

item.title: DOJ tests limits of never-before-used court to deport suspected terrorist
item.description: The Alien Terrorist Removal Court was created by Congress in 1996 and signed into law by President Bill Clinton. Before now, it had never been used.

item.title: FDA panel recommends loosening regulations for some peptides
item.description: The FDA panel reviewed seven peptides to decide if they should be added to a list of substances that can be safely produced by compounding pharmacies.

item.title: Kouri Richins: Behind the Facade | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Natalie Morales discuss the case of Kouri Richins, a Utah mom who was sentenced to life in prison without parole for murdering her husband, on Post Mortem after two trial jurors break down their take on the evidence.

item.title: The Man with Two Names | Post Mortem
item.description: Anne-Marie Green sits down with "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty and producer Josh Yager to discuss Jon Green, who was arrested for stealing his ex-wife's dogs and convicted in 2025 for soliciting her murder. But Erin and Josh first met Jon Green back in 2002, when he was then known as Ted Maher, and he had been convicted of arson, leading to the deaths of billionaire Edmond Safra and his nurse.

item.title: Beverly Hills 911 | Post Mortem
item.description: CBS News correspondent Tracy Smith and "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty discuss the case of 67-year-old Violet Yacobi, who was found dead by her children in her Beverly Hills mansion.

item.title: The Love Bombing of Gloria Choi | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Natalie Morales discuss Gloria Choi's murder. The single mother was shot by her ex-boyfriend, Billy Rickman.

item.title: The Killing of Theresa Fusco | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Erin Moriarty discuss the cases of Theresa Fusco, Kelly Morrissey, and Jackie Martarella, who went missing more than 40 years ago in Long Island, New York.

item.title: Jade Colvin is Missing | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Natalie Morales discuss the case of Jade Colvin, a 14-year-old who went missing after running away from the Iowa foster care system.

item.title: Kimberly Langwell's Hidden Grave | Post Mortem
item.description: Join "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Peter Van Sant as they discuss the case of Kim Langwell, who was missing for more than two decades until her body was discovered under the floor of her ex-boyfriend's house.

item.title: The Root Beer Float Murder | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Peter Van Sant discuss the murder of Harold Allen, who was poisoned with a root beer float by his wife and her daughter.

item.title: Glen Hansard: Once and always a street musician
item.description: The Irish singer-songwriter behind "Once," The Frames and The Swell Season, talks about his first solo album, "Rhythm and Repose."
